coursePurpose: Senior transition course for sustainable lifelong movement, independent decision-making, evidence literacy, safety, accessibility, leadership, and postsecondary wellbeing planning.

weeks.title: Senior fitness baseline & self-direction
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a graduating senior use evidence, autonomy, safety, accessibility, and realistic constraints to make durable decisions about senior fitness baseline & self-direction?
weeks.scenario: A Grade 12 learner must make or defend a realistic decision involving senior fitness baseline & self-direction while balancing time, resources, access, safety, and long-term sustainability.
weeks.model: Define the goal; inspect evidence; identify constraints; choose a safe and inclusive action; monitor a meaningful indicator; revise transparently.

days.concept: Use senior-level exercise science, decision-making, evidence, safety, accessibility, and self-management to examine senior fitness baseline & self-direction.
days.workedExample: A senior reviews a realistic senior fitness baseline & self-direction case, identifies useful evidence and constraints, chooses a safe and inclusive response, and revises the decision when new information appears.
days.independentTask: Create a concise investigate response for senior fitness baseline & self-direction with evidence, one limitation, one practical adaptation, and a next-step decision.
days.successCriteria: I can make and defend a practical lifelong-movement decision using evidence, safety, access, ethics, and revision.
days.instruction: Examine senior fitness baseline & self-direction as a transition-to-adulthood movement and wellbeing problem.
days.practice: Apply the principle to a fictional, household, school, work, recreation, or community context without requiring private health information.
days.evidence: Preserve reasoning, source/evidence used, limitation, adaptation, and revision.

weeks.title: First-aid decision principles

days.concept: Use senior-level exercise science, decision-making, evidence, safety, accessibility, and self-management to examine first-aid decision principles.

days.successCriteria: I can make and defend a practical lifelong-movement decision using evidence, safety, access, ethics, and revision.
days.instruction: Examine first-aid decision principles as a transition-to-adulthood movement and wellbeing problem.

days.evidence: Preserve reasoning, source/evidence used, limitation, adaptation, and revision.

weeks.title: Independent activity practicum

weeks.model: Define the goal; inspect evidence; identify constraints; choose a safe and inclusive action; monitor a meaningful indicator; revise transparently.

weeks.title: Lifetime movement portfolio & transition
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a graduating senior use evidence, autonomy, safety, accessibility, and realistic constraints to make durable decisions about lifetime movement portfolio & transition?
weeks.scenario: A Grade 12 learner must make or defend a realistic decision involving lifetime movement portfolio & transition while balancing time, resources, access, safety, and long-term sustainability.
weeks.model: Define the goal; inspect evidence; identify constraints; choose a safe and inclusive action; monitor a meaningful indicator; revise transparently.
